title: He, the mobile, te & getting ready
summary: il = he: il veut. le portable = the mobile phone. When 'you' is the object (I see you, I want you), use te instead of tu. This also gives you reflexive verbs: Tu dois te préparer (You must get ready), Je dois me préparer (I must get ready).
points: il = he: il veut, il peut, il doit.
le portable = mobile phone (in France). It's masculine even though it ends in e.
tu = you as the subject (you want). te = you as the object (I want you): Je dois te préparer.
te / me become t' / m' before a vowel: Je veux t'inviter.
'Get ready' = 'prepare yourself': Tu dois te préparer, Je dois me préparer.
'Relax' is also reflexive: Tu dois te relaxer. The re- has no accent, so it's soft.
Focus on one piece of the sentence at a time. Don't jump ahead.
drills: She can invite him to the birthday party.
Elle peut l'inviter à la fête d'anniversaire.
Do you want to invite him?
